newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Alleged "British spy" to be treated, then tried.
newsitem.headline: Alleged "British spy" to be treated, then tried.

text.p: Russian judges reviewing the case of a junior foreign ministry official alleged to have spied for Britain ruled on Wednesday he would stand trial but only after undergoing psychiatric treatment, a court official said.

She said the judges ruled in favour of prosecutors who say Platon Obukhov is mentally unstable now, but was sane at the time of the alleged crime. It was not immediately clear how long his treatment would take and whether the defence would appeal.

A second secretary in the Foreign Ministry's prestigious North America Department and a writer of pulp spy thrillers on the side, Obukhov has been held since April 1996 on charges he was paid for information by British MI6 agents.
A lawyer for Obukhov said on Tuesday that judges at the Moscow City Court declined to accept documents attesting Obukhov was not mentally fit to stand trial.

The lawyer and his parents insist he has been mentally unstable since childhood and is unfit to stand trial. They want him discharged to a psychiatric hospital. The judges earlier rejected an appeal that Obukhov's parents be appointed his legal guardians.
Criminal proceedings against Obukhov, 28, could have been dropped if the court had decided that he was unfit.
